parsedVerdict.reasoning:
OrderService is an application-layer use-case service. It does application work: it loads aggregates through the repository interfaces declared in the domain, calls domain behaviour (Order.advanceTo, Order.cancel, Product.reserve, Product.release), saves the results and maps aggregates to DTOs. It has no transport code (no HTTP or request/response handling), no framework code and no concrete persistence code (no SQL, no file or database access).

Borderline items:
- The stock check before reserving runs across several Product aggregates so that no stock changes unless every item can be reserved. That kind of all-or-nothing check across aggregates is legitimate use-case orchestration.
- combineItems merges duplicate products and checks that each item has a product id and a positive integer quantity. This is mostly input validation at the use-case boundary. The rule "an order requires at least one item" would ideally live in the Order aggregate, but checking it here is not clearly a responsibility of a different layer kind.
- The in-memory nextId counter generates ids in a simple way, but it is not persistence or transport logic.

None of these clearly belongs to a different layer kind, so the file is judged consistent with its declared application role.
